# Die Kette

This project follows the rules of Die Kette. Agents read `.kette/profile.json` first and apply rules in this order: company overlays, platform, stack, architecture patterns, core. A core rule applies unless an ADR explicitly overrides it.

## Flow for every change
Apply small fixes (a typo, one line) directly and check them with step 4. Everything else runs like this, each role as its own subagent:

1. Requirements: `design-system-agents:requirements-engineer` writes testable requirements with IDs.
2. Architecture: `design-system-agents:software-architect` picks the pattern (skill `architecture-patterns`), cuts modules and interfaces and records hard-to-reverse decisions as ADRs in `docs/adr/`.
3. Implementation: `design-system-agents:fullstack-developer` builds in small, tested steps following `engineering-rules` and `platform-profile`.
4. Required gates, independent of the implementation:
   - `kette-engineering:code-reviewer` checks the diff against core rules, patterns and the project profile.
   - `design-system-agents:qa-engineer` verifies every requirement with evidence.
   - For UI changes also `design-review-pack:design-reviewer` and `design-review-pack:ux-reviewer`, and where keyboard, contrast, focus or screen readers are affected, `design-system-agents:accessibility-manager`.
5. Findings go back to the role that caused them (skill `evidence-and-defect-routing`), then the gate checks again. A change is done only when all gates pass.

A whole feature with all roles, fix loop and run log: `/feature-loop start <feature>` (in Claude Code `/design-system-agents:feature-loop`).

Several branches in the same round (batch review): describe the round to `/feature-loop`, for example `/feature-loop filter and export done, review at the end`. Builders check themselves against the rules and the probes in `.review/probes/`, without gates per branch or per fix. All branches go onto one release branch, the gates from step 4 run once on it, in parallel (the batch takes `codeReviewer: kette-engineering:code-reviewer` and `gates: [qa, accessibility]` next to design and UX review), then one fix round and a re-check of only the failed findings. At most 4 heavy agents (browsers, simulators, builds) run at once. The round is done when the review on the release branch passes.

The agents, gates and `/feature-loop` need Die Kette on the machine (`kette login <key>`). Without them, patterns and ADRs, `engineering-rules` while building and the check with `kette-engineering-core:kette-check` still apply, and `kette doctor` shows what is missing.

Credentials and access go through the secret wallet (skill `secret-wallet`, `.kette/wallet.json`): declare new variables there, start commands with `kette wallet run`, never put a value into code, a file in the repo or the chat.

Create infrastructure only as code and check it with plan or what-if. A human runs apply, deploys and destructive migrations.

## Where the rules live
- On this machine in `~/.kette/bundles/enterprise/`: `rules/`, `profiles/`, `checks/`.
- In Claude Code the plugins `kette-engineering-core@kette-enterprise`, `kette-engineering@kette-enterprise`, `design-system-agents@kette-enterprise`, `design-review-pack@kette-enterprise`, `kette-ticketing@kette-enterprise`, enabled for this project in `.claude/settings.json`.
- Browse with `kette rules`, plugin contents and checks with `kette doctor`.
- Settings this project inherits from its Kette instance (ticketing, wallet, overlays, stations): read them with `kette profile --effective` before ticket, wallet or review work, the values of the repo win.
